To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the potency of a music piece is related to the roughness of its sound and the loudness of its instruments.

(i) arousal and valence are the dominant dimensions of affective quality for the stimuli used here; (ii) the potency dimension can be related to musical features, in particular to Roughness, Spectral Flux and Loudness; and (iii) the tension dimension cannot be related to any of the musical features considered here.
the affective qualities of classical music can be clustered beyond the valence-arousal plane, and that the affective potency dimension can be captured through musical features.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of musical features that are related to affective dimensions other then valence and arousal.
the identification and characterization of musical features related to the potency and tension dimensions, and with the assessment of the role played by the tempo and mode in this relationship.
the affective qualities of classical music, and in particular with their representation in terms of the four dimensions of valence, arousal, potency and tension, as defined by Russell (2003)
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the arousal dimension is a very strong predictor of the affective quality of a musical excerpt.
valence and arousal are the most important affective dimensions for music, but that potency can play a role, in particular in the case of fast music with high loudness and spectral flux.
arousal and valence dimensions are still the most important ones for representing and recognizing emotions in music, while other dimensions such as potency can play a role as well.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the valence and the arousal dimensions are still the most important dimensions to represent and to predict affective qualities in musical stimuli.
we have shown that the affective potency of music is related to a combination of musical features that are not necessarily related to valence and arousal.
the potency dimension is a significant component of music affective space and it can be captured by a few musical features, which can be easily computed from real music recordings.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the affective potency of music is a multidimensional construct, and not a simple linear dimension, as it is often assumed.

, although the valence and the arousal dimensions are the most important ones for the description of affective qualities, the use of a wider set of features can help to better characterize the affective space of music.
the valence and potency dimensions are more strongly correlated than the valence and tension dimensions.
